question: Why do people who know what is beneficial still commit quickly pleasing sins?
premises: Some people know what is beneficial.
Those same people can be deluded.
Sins may appear to give happiness quickly.
inference: Delusion can override knowledge when sinful acts promise immediate pleasure.
uncertainties: The specific agents beyond 'people' are not named in this verse.
plain_english: Even those who know what is beneficial, when deluded, are drawn to sins that quickly give pleasure.
